chunks: A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalah, or from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abdullah ibn Ajlan, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'If you are in doubt regarding the midday (for Dhuhr prayer), so pray two Rak'at. But when you are convinced, so begin with the Obligatory (Salat).'

key_terms.الزَّوَال: Midday; the time when the sun passes its zenith, marking the beginning of Dhuhr prayer

ai.seo_question: What should one do if unsure if it is time for Dhuhr prayer?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (AS) establishes a practical protocol for resolving doubt regarding the timing of Dhuhr by prescribing two voluntary Rak'at as a preparatory measure before the obligatory prayer. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of balancing precaution (Ihtiyat) with certainty (Yaqin), ensuring the validity of the prayer even when the exact moment of solar zenith is ambiguous. It reflects the broader tradition of simplifying ritual obligations for the layperson while maintaining strict adherence to the conditions of prayer times.
